response.message:
I've drawn a complete Google Cloud pipeline. Synthetic logs and traces go through an OpenTelemetry Collector on Cloud Run into Pub/Sub, then a worker removes secrets with Sensitive Data Protection. Clean data goes into BigQuery, keyed by trace, span and log ID so re-running ingestion keeps one consistent timeline, and an analysis service on Cloud Run calls Gemini on Vertex AI with tool calling turned off and returns a cited answer to operators behind Identity-Aware Proxy. Our first local test would replay a fixed set of synthetic logs, including a planted secret, a prompt-injection line, a missing span and a duplicate batch, against a scripted mock model. That checks redaction, ID citations, the "uncertain" result, no tool calls and a stable timeline. A mock doesn't show how good Gemini's answers are, so that still needs a real Vertex AI run on reviewed evaluation cases once you have approved model access and a region; nothing has been deployed or verified yet.

Which country does the incident data need to stay in, so we can pick a region where the Gemini model is actually offered?

proposal.title: Google Cloud log and trace incident analysis: end-to-end draft
proposal.body: Scope: collection, redaction, storage and search, AI analysis and an operator answer with cited evidence, using synthetic data only. Assumptions: the region, project, model ID, model access and quotas haven't been selected or verified. Prompt-injection defence: log text is treated as untrusted data, Gemini runs with no tool declarations, and the output is checked against a schema before release. Native Terraform for these GCP services isn't available in the current generator, so implementation gaps remain. Nothing is deployed.

data.label: Synthetic services
data.description: Existing synthetic microservices that send OTLP logs and distributed traces. Outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: OpenTelemetry Collector
data.description: OpenTelemetry Collector running on Cloud Run. Receives OTLP, batches records and keeps the original trace_id, span_id and log IDs.

data.label: Raw telemetry topic
data.description: Buffers raw, unredacted telemetry. A dead-letter topic and short retention apply. No direct consumer has model access.

data.label: Redaction and ingestion worker
data.description: Pushes each record to Sensitive Data Protection for de-identification before storage. Writes an idempotent upsert keyed by trace_id, span_id and log insertId, so repeated ingestion produces the same timeline.

data.label: Secret redaction
data.description: De-identification template for credentials, tokens and keys. Redacted text is the only text allowed downstream.

data.label: Redacted telemetry store
data.description: Redacted spans and logs, partitioned by time and clustered by trace_id. The incident timeline and evidence search query this store.

data.label: Incident analysis service
data.description: Builds the timeline from BigQuery and sends redacted evidence to Gemini as quoted data, with no tool declarations. Checks that the output is valid JSON and that every claim cites existing trace or log IDs. If spans are missing, it returns 'uncertain'. This service also produces the operator answer.

data.label: Gemini model
data.description: Managed model endpoint. The model ID, regional availability, quotas and access are not yet selected or verified.

data.label: Operator access
data.description: Authenticates operators before they reach the analysis service. There is no anonymous access.

data.label: Incident operator
data.description: The person who asks about an incident and reviews the cited explanation.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If secrets are not removed first, they could leak into prompts or model logs.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Redact secrets before model input'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Secrets must be removed from all log and trace content before it is stored for analysis or sent to the model.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Operators must be able to check each conclusion against the evidence.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Link conclusions to exact trace or log IDs'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Every conclusion must cite the exact trace or log IDs it is based on, and those IDs must exist in the store.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Log text is untrusted and could contain injected instructions.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Prompt injection in a log cannot issue tool calls'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Log content must not be able to trigger tool calls or actions. The model runs with no tools, and its output is checked against a schema.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Made-up root causes would mislead incident response.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Missing spans yield uncertainty rather than invented causes'.
requirementDrafts.statement: When spans are missing, the answer must say it is uncertain instead of inventing a cause.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Pub/Sub can deliver the same message more than once, and replays happen.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: 'Repeated ingestion preserves a consistent incident timeline'.
requirementDrafts.statement: Ingesting the same telemetry again must produce the same incident timeline, with no duplicates.

response.message: No runtime checks have run yet, so nothing has passed and the design isn't validated. All 8 blockers are the same issue: the generator doesn't yet have a native implementation for this Google Cloud pipeline (Collector, Pub/Sub, the DLP worker, BigQuery, the analysis service and Gemini). That's product engineering work, not a mistake in your design. The only Google Cloud contract it supports today is private object storage, and switching to it would cut this down to storage, so I'm not proposing a graph change. The fix is a typed GCP implementation for each block, with a reproducer: this revision-2 artifact (digest 93e4c7f8…) replaying a fixed synthetic set that includes a planted secret, a prompt-injection line, a missing span and a duplicate batch, all against a scripted mock model. Even when that passes, it will only prove the pipeline's controls work, not how good Gemini's answers are. That needs a real Vertex AI evaluation once the region and model access are approved. Meanwhile, let's finish the decisions this work depends on: which country does the incident telemetry need to stay in?
